title: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pulled Pork Sandwiches with Mustard Slaw
dek: Fork-tender cider-braised pork shoulder, crisp mustard slaw, dill pickles and pickled red onions pile into toasted rolls for a make-ahead slow-cooker dinner.
image_alt: Pulled pork sandwich topped with creamy cabbage slaw, dill pickles and pickled red onion
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, trimmed and cut into 4 equal chunks
1 cup unsweetened apple cider, not apple cider vinegar
5 cups shredded green cabbage-and-carrot slaw mix

instructions.name: Season the pork
instructions.text: Thaw the pork completely in the refrigerator if frozen. Pat the chunks dry, trim only thick surface fat and season all over with 2 teaspoons salt and the pepper. Cutting the shoulder into four even pieces keeps the cook time predictable without making the meat so small that it dries out.

instructions.name: Brown for a savory base
instructions.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the pork in two batches, about 2 minutes on each broad side, then transfer it to a 6-quart slow cooker. This step adds flavor but can be skipped when time is tight.

instructions.name: Build the cider braise
instructions.text: Scatter the onion and garlic around the pork. Whisk the apple cider, chicken broth, 2 tablespoons vinegar, tomato paste, brown sugar, 1 tablespoon Dijon, Worcestershire, paprika and thyme, then pour the mixture around the meat. Turn the chunks once to coat, keeping the slow cooker no more than two-thirds full.

instructions.name: Slow-cook until shreddable
instructions.text: Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours without lifting the lid, until the pork is fork-tender and several chunks register 195 to 205°F in their centers. Pork is safe at 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest, but shoulder needs the higher range for its collagen to soften enough to shred. Follow your model manual if its capacity or settings differ.

instructions.name: Rest, reduce and shred
instructions.text: Transfer the pork to a rimmed board and rest 10 minutes. Skim excess fat from the cooker, then pour 2 cups cooking liquid into a wide saucepan and simmer over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until reduced to about 1 1/4 cups. Shred the pork, discarding large fat pockets, and moisten it with the reduced sauce.

instructions.name: Make the mustard slaw
instructions.text: While the pork rests, whisk mayonnaise, the remaining 2 tablespoons vinegar, the remaining 1 tablespoon Dijon, honey and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Add the cabbage-and-carrot mix and toss until evenly coated. Let stand 10 minutes, then toss again.

instructions.name: Toast and assemble
instructions.text: Toast the cut sides of the rolls under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes, watching continuously. Divide the sauced pork among the bottom buns, then top with mustard slaw, dill pickle slices and drained pickled red onions. Close the sandwiches and serve immediately.

why_it_works: Pork shoulder has enough connective tissue to stay juicy through a long LOW cook; the 195 to 205°F finishing range turns that collagen into gelatin for clean shredding.
Apple cider contributes fruit and acidity while broth supplies enough savory liquid for an even braise; reducing a measured portion concentrates the sauce without making the sandwiches soggy.
Cool mustard slaw, tart pickles and pickled onion cut through the rich pork, and toasted rolls provide a barrier against the braising juices.
swaps: Use a 4- to 4 1/2-pound bone-in pork shoulder; keep the same liquid amounts and remove the bone before shredding.
Replace the apple cider with cloudy unsweetened apple juice. Do not replace it cup-for-cup with vinegar, which would make the braise harsh.
For a dairy-free sandwich, use dairy-free mayonnaise and rolls; check the Worcestershire label for fish if serving anyone who avoids anchovies.
storage: Refrigerate pork and slaw in separate airtight containers within 2 hours. Keep the pork up to 4 days and the slaw up to 2 days. Reheat pork with a splash of broth in a covered saucepan over medium-low heat until it reaches 165°F; assemble on freshly toasted rolls. Freeze the cooled pork with some sauce for up to 3 months, but do not freeze the slaw or assembled sandwiches.
notes: Always thaw pork before slow cooking; frozen meat can spend too long warming through the food-safety danger zone.
Slow cookers vary. Begin checking at 7 1/2 hours, but use both temperature and fork tenderness rather than the clock alone.
Do not pack a slow cooker above the fill line in its manual. This recipe is written for a 6-quart model and should remain no more than two-thirds full.
Keep the slaw, pickles and onions separate until serving so the rolls stay crisp.

faqs.q: Can I cook the pork on HIGH?
faqs.a: Yes. Cook on HIGH for about 4 1/2 to 5 hours, then verify several chunks are fork-tender and in the 195 to 205°F shredding range. LOW gives the widest margin for an evenly tender result.

faqs.q: Why is my pulled pork tough instead of shreddable?
faqs.a: It usually needs more time. If the center is safely above 145°F but the meat resists a fork, cover and continue on LOW in 30-minute increments until the collagen softens and the chunks separate easily.

faqs.q: Can I make the sandwiches ahead for a party?
faqs.a: Prepare the pork up to 3 days ahead and reheat it to 165°F with reserved sauce. Mix the slaw up to 4 hours ahead, but toast and assemble the rolls just before serving to prevent sogginess.
